text: Two-moderator sign-off: Evie reviews first, any other moderator can give the second approval, and Evie can flag a story as needing a third
notes:
Design: each record carries an approvals list (who, when) and a requiresThird flag. "Approved" becomes a computed state — two signatures, or three when flagged — rather than a status someone sets. The dashboard shows where each story is: "Reviewed by Evie, waiting for one more."

Open question for the team: when Evie is away, does anyone else get to do the first review, or does the queue wait? Proposed: first review is hers by default, any moderator can take it, and the log shows who did.

text: Stop bot and spoof submissions: add Cloudflare Turnstile to the submit button and the gate
answer: A captcha helps, and the right one is nearly free for us. Turnstile is Cloudflare's — we are already there — and it is invisible to real people: no puzzles, one script on the page and one check on the server when a story is submitted. The moderation queue is still the real defence (nothing publishes without a person); Turnstile keeps the queue from filling with junk.
notes: Also worth adding: a per-IP rate limit on /api/submit, and a size cap that already exists on uploads.

text: Shorter removal code, and email it to the contributor by default
answer: Shorter is easy. Emailing by default means asking for an email on every submission, and today email is optional and only collected when someone ticks "the team can contact me" — that was a deliberate privacy choice. Proposed middle: the email field is always visible, labelled "so we can send you your removal code", still optional; if they skip it the code shows on screen as now. Nobody has to hand over an email to tell their story.
notes: Needs an outbound email path we do not have yet (Resend or Postmark; a few dollars a month). Same path would carry the "your story is live" note later.

text: A very basic video editor in the recorder: add to a recording at a point you choose, or cut a stretch out of it
notes:
Matthew asked for guided, CapCut-style submissions. Scoped down to two operations that cover most of what people actually need after a first take: insert (record a new segment and drop it in at the playhead — "I forgot to say") and cut (drag a start and end on the timeline, remove it — "ignore that bit"). No transitions, no captions, no music.

How it would work: every take is kept as its own clip; the editor is a list of clips with in/out points under a single scrub bar. Playback stitches them in the browser. On "Add to the archive" the clips are rendered to one file in the browser (ffmpeg.wasm, ~30MB loaded once at that moment) so the archive, the transcription and the player all still get a single recording. Retake-from-here falls out of this for free.

Audio submissions get the same two operations with the same code.

text: Name fields: the first-name box is too wide and the gap between first and last name is wrong
notes: Both names are single-column fields in the form grid, so on a wide modal they stretch. Cap each at a sensible width and tighten the gap. Fifteen minutes; goes out with the next push.

text: Guided submissions: prompts beside the recorder ("Where were you? What did you see first?") so people know what to say
notes: The other half of Matthew's CapCut note. Cheap on its own: a small card of prompts next to the recorder, optional, that the contributor can step through. Worth deciding whether the prompts are the team's questions (what an interviewer would ask) or a loose structure (beginning, what happened, afterwards). Needs Matthew and Evie's words, not mine.
